question: Does actual Human motion variation stably precede/coincide with instantaneous cuff-force change and explain cumulative burden?
evidence: archive-only exploratory diagnosis; existing same-Human development traces; repeats are not independent samples
time_basis: absolute physics time and task time t_abs-10.05, independently confirmed per case; never host wall time
metrics: 5ms left force integral; native raw dq gradients edge_order=2; combined Euclidean TV, acceleration variation, jerk RMS/p95/max; phase-local independent aggregation
lag_convention: corr(motion[t],force[t+lag]); positive lag means motion leads force; ±1s; no crossing phase boundaries

sensitivity.null: within-phase circular shifts excluding ±2s; maximum absolute lag correlation; descriptive only

phase2_gate: Only stable time-local correspondence with consistent direction/lag across B/18D and OUTBOUND/RETURN plus contrasts may motivate bounded physical sensitivity. Pooled correlation, cumulative slope, or isolated peak cannot pass this gate. Otherwise branch D; unsupported exact temporal interface additionally branch E.
thresholds: all original qualification thresholds unchanged; no new diagnostic score used for candidate promotion
stop: No stable coupling -> stop waypoint/speed expansion, preserve all outcomes, study tracking/allocator/replan mechanisms.
